simple.meaning: חָשֻׁם (Châshum) is a Hebrew word meaning “Chashum , the name of two or three Israelites.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חָשֻׁם (H2828) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ezra 2:19, with occurrences in Ezra, Nehemiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָשֻׁם (H2828) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חָשֻׁם (H2828) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חָשֻׁם (Châshum) / H2828 is traced through Ezra 2:19, Ezra 10:33, Nehemiah 7:22, Nehemiah 8:4 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: Chashum , the name of two or three Israelites
definitions.full: H2828. Chashum חָשֻׁם proper name, masculine head of a family of returned exiles Ezra 2:19 = Neh 7:22 ; Ezra 10:33 compare Neh 8:4 ; 10:19 .

occurrences.englishText: The children of Hashum, two hundred twenty-three.
Of the sons of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, Shimei.

Ezra the scribe stood on a pulpit of wood, which they had made for the purpose; and beside him stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, on his right hand; and on his left hand, Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
